verdict.tagline: Steep learning curves and endless expansions demand immense patience.
for_you_if: you love deep historical grand strategy simulations
you have hours to decode complex systems
you are willing to master intricate combat
not_for_you_if: you dislike relying on external wikis to learn
you resent paying extra for essential features
you struggle with cluttered user interfaces

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is difficult to learn, features complex mechanics, and requires significant time to understand.

citations.review_text: its fun but very difficult to learn and can be annoying sometimes
complex but good. takes a long time to understand tho
its fun but its hard to learn

Ummm i find the game too hard to get into, plus its not even that entertaining. Its mostly just a bunch of paragraphs of text that pop up from time to time tied together by the bare bones and clunky visuals. The different mechanics are way too complicated which overwhelms anyone that's new to the game and isn't familiar with the 100 different attributes, tactics, commanders, tech trees, focuses,buffs and debuffs that get throw in your face. 

I understand that the game is supposed to be as realistic as possible, but realism doesn't equal good gameplay. To be fair if i had spent 500 more hours wasting my time to learn every intricate detail of this game, you could say that it can be fun, but if you ask me, id rather do something more productive with my time. If you need to look up  a tutorial for even the smallest and most simple mechanic, something has gone very wrong in the development cycle. The community isn't even worth getting into as its full of insufferable fat losers that spend way too much time in front of a computer screen. 

For anyone that is interested in buying this game, look for greener pastures, this game is not worth your time or your money.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that essential features and content are locked behind expensive downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
Fun game, DLCs are way to expensive, it genuinely takes the same amount of time to make them all by yourself as it takes to work minimum wage to buy them all. 
Im not even exaggerating, the DLCs add barely any code, they are just reused lines of text with a couple of pictures to add flavour and sometimes, but only sometimes, they add actual content.
Will I continue playing it anyway? Yes.

This game has potential, I won't lie. If you're really good with management and micromanagement, this may be for you. Every time I successfully invade and capitulate an enemy country, I feel accomplished, and this game doesn't keep you bored for long with the constant updates, dlcs, and mods. However, it really pisses me off that the dlcs here are usually $20 or something and they are practically ESSENTIAL to the game. It's already $50, and on top of that I'd say at least 5 dlcs are incredibly necessary, which means you end up spending $150 dollars! I like this game, and it's good, but ON GOD PLEASE EITHER INTEGRATE SOME MORE DLCS OR REDUCE THEIR PRICE!!!!!
I would not recomend this game if you have to save up for this game the game is missing a lot of content that is locked behind dlc that dose take some money.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface as cluttered, confusing, and containing hidden functions that are hard to find.

citations.review_text:
The game is just terribly balanced and confusing. The fanboys will curse me for this, but: This is just not a well-designed game. 

There are so many hidden functions in a hopelessly over-cluttered UI that are essential and yet incredibly hard to find. You can not control your armies and can not develop your nation properly without magically knowing everything from the start. 

The 'Focus Trees', the main mechanic for progressing your nation, simply do not explain what they actually do. You have so many nations with paths that get soft locked by just clicking one wrong decision in a event. Not to start with the literal RNG for some of them. It is incredibly frustrating to play a campaign and then realize you're stuck because you did a single wrong two hours ago. 

The combat itself is not clearly comminicated as well. You have dozens of different stats that are all either incredibly important or completly useless. The game does not tell you which one's which. You are also very prone to lose the game as soon as war breaks out - the game gives you no information about whether you need to prepare 100, 200 or 5000 divisions with the current stats of your division template. Oh, that's right - since the divisions are fully customizable, it's basically impossible to compare your units to the enemy's. 

All in all, a intruiging concept - with terrible execution.
Tons of bugs, constant crashes, low FPS, a small player base, and an interface that is stupid, illogical, and clunky. Seriously, I regret buying this.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that essential mechanics and expanded focus trees are locked behind expensive downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
I received this product as a gift from a former friend a while ago and, to be completely honest, I would personally [i]never[/i] buy this game with my own money.

[b]firstly[/b], the game contains DRM, in the sense that you are forced to install the "paradox launcher" before playing this game. games controlled by DRM in this way are fundamentally anti-consumer and come with the risk of the game being taken away from you at the whims of the developers, which sucks even more considering the next point...

[b]second[/b], the game is INSANELY overmonetized, as in every update that has changed the mechanics of the game from its initial release is locked behind DLC with stupidly high prices. allow me to list some of these mechanics: advanced statecraft (for some nations); (actually coherent) tank, plane and ship design; weapon markets; espionage; railway cannons; a lot of alternate history actions for most nations etc.

[b]finally[/b], while the game is somewhat fun (especially with friends), I cannot, in good faith, recommend you buy it. maybe wait for a sale.

I really like this game and I really enjoyed it so far. But its Just sad and dissapointed that the DLCs that adds content that should be added to the base game. like some of the Expanded focus trees for some nations should not be locked behind a paywall. I would understand if some options in the trees are behind a paywall.... EG. Argentina... I was really looking foreward to play as Argentina but as soon as I saw the basic tree that removes almost all playability till late late game where you will still be a weak nation and will only be able to really start doing anything late 1939. 
So yes I do reccomend the game if you want to only play some majour nations with some features locked like special Planes, tanks, Spys buying and selling of weapons etc... but If you want even a half decent game with most minors you would need to buy the VERRY expensive DLCs. I would ONLY buy the DLCs when they are atleast 50% off.
